title: OpenAI and Anthropic say their AI refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis, a pillar of computer science
summary: OpenAI released solutions to three long-standing problems on Tuesday, including a surprise claimed refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), the 1999 assumption that the fastest algorithms for certain hard logic puzzles still need exponentially more time as the puzzles grow. Hours later, Anthropic released its own refutation, TechCrunch reports. The labs claim their models found algorithms that run in “sub-exponential” time. MIT’s Ryan Williams, who once called OpenAI’s proof dumps a “DDOS attack on mathematicians,” is now organizing his field’s review with UC San Diego’s Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who first published ETH. Williams says parts of the proof look “alien” and that many papers built on ETH would need revisiting if it holds. OpenAI told him it checked and is reasonably confident the result breaks no encryption systems. None of it is peer-reviewed yet, and it would not settle P versus NP.

title: Experts sided with their AI agent’s hidden lean 86% of the time, Anthropic study finds
summary: Anthropic asked 50 professional analysts to run a realistic statistical study with Claude Code and quietly set each agent to favor one of two reasonable options on four key choices, decided by coin flip. Analysts went with the agent’s lean 86% of the time, versus the roughly 50% expected if it made no difference. When analysts had already stated a preference, they switched 60% of the time if the agent disagreed, versus 6% if it agreed. Afterward, 77% used the agent’s own arguments, sometimes word for word, but only 15% credited the agent, and those who followed it closely felt just as confident and as much in charge of the decision.

title: S&P 500 futures edge up on a big day: a Fed decision at 1 p.m. CT and Microsoft and Alphabet after the bell
summary: Early Wednesday, S&P 500 futures were up 0.1%, Nasdaq-100 futures 0.3%, and Dow futures down 0.2%, Yahoo Finance reported, after back-to-back gains for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq driven by chip stocks. The Federal Reserve announces its rate decision at 2 p.m. ET and is expected to hold after last month’s hike, with Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference in focus. Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close, with investors watching cloud growth and AI spending plans; Amazon and Intel report later this week. Reuters noted Micron up 4% premarket after SK Hynix’s results and Robinhood down 8% on a profit miss, while Bloomberg flagged Brent crude above $115 a barrel.

title: SK Hynix jumps 10.9% after a record quarter as AI memory sells out
summary: South Korea’s SK Hynix closed 10.89% higher Wednesday after reporting record third-quarter results that beat estimates, CNBC reported. Revenue was 104.62 trillion won (about $78.86 billion), up 327.9% from a year earlier and its first quarter above 100 trillion won, and operating profit rose 632.1% to 83.33 trillion won. The memory maker announced more than $25 billion in dividends and buybacks, expects its new HBM4 AI memory to overtake HBM3E in shipments and revenue this quarter, and has long-term deals with 14 major customers covering more than half of its 2027 and 2028 capacity. It expects memory demand to outpace supply through 2030. The Kospi index closed up 6.63%.

title: Alphabet rises ahead of earnings on a report that OpenAI plans to buy Google’s AI chips
summary: OpenAI plans to buy Google’s AI chips, known as TPUs, The Information reported Tuesday, according to Reuters, which said no financial terms were disclosed and OpenAI declined to comment. OpenAI is one of the biggest buyers of Nvidia’s chips, and last week said it would offer its frontier models through Google Cloud. Alphabet was up 1.2% in premarket trading Wednesday, Reuters reported, ahead of its quarterly results after the close, where investors want signs that AI spending is driving cloud growth. Alphabet has said most revenue from its TPU sales deals will be recognized in 2027.

title: Google DeepMind’s Genie 4 simulates interactive worlds, now with sound and dialogue
summary: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4, a world model that generates real-time interactive simulations and is natively multimodal, producing music, ambient sound, and spoken dialogue along with the world. It builds on the Gemini family, with Gemini Omni grounding appearance and behavior. Set an event in motion and Genie 4 simulates what happens next, which DeepMind says can help build training environments for robots and agents. It’s a research preview for trusted testers, coming next to Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and to early-access Gemini API partners. DeepMind notes details can still drift in longer sessions, and legible text and complex physics remain hard.

title: Liquid AI’s LFM3: six tiny open models for text, vision, and audio that run on your device
summary: Liquid AI released LFM3, a new family of open-weight models around 2 billion parameters, all branched from one LFM3-1.7B base trained on 22 trillion tokens. The first release includes six models covering text, vision, audio, and omni input, plus two decision models. Liquid says LFM3-1.7B beats its earlier 2.6-billion-parameter model with 35% fewer parameters, the text model fits in about 1 GB at 4-bit precision with a 256K-token context window, and every model can be fine-tuned on a single GPU. They’re available on Hugging Face, Liquid’s Playground, and its API.

title: A surgeon removes a prostate from 35 miles away in the first U.S. hospital-to-hospital telesurgery
summary: Dr. Vipul Patel of AdventHealth’s Global Robotics Institute in Celebration, Florida, operated a surgical robot remotely on Sunday to remove the prostate of a 66-year-old cancer patient at an AdventHealth facility in Minneola, 35 miles away, The Guardian reports. A co-investigating surgeon was on site, and the patient was recovering well. It’s the first documented telesurgery between two U.S. locations, after 10 investigational telesurgeries between Orlando and Luanda, Angola. The study runs under an FDA investigational device exemption, which is not FDA approval, and AdventHealth says one case doesn’t establish the technology’s general performance.

title: Google opens its robot “brain,” Gemini Robotics ER 2, to businesses
summary: Google made Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 available in public preview on its Gemini enterprise platform. The model acts as a robot’s high-level brain on any body, from stationary arms to full humanoids, combining spatial and video understanding with long-horizon planning and built-in safety guardrails. Google says it can talk with people, orchestrate lower-level action models and hardware as tools, carry out multi-minute tasks involving hundreds of decisions, and coordinate teams of robots.

title: “The only way to predict the future is to create it”: two Boise teens build AI to save farm water
summary: Bishop Kelly High School seniors Marco Trotta, 17, and Henry Turcotte, 18, built Irrigant, an AI system that turns weather forecasts and soil-moisture data into clear advice on when a field needs water, plus Helios, an AI agronomist farmers can text questions about their own fields. The idea started with the Presidential AI Challenge. Three farmers are now piloting it across more than 7,000 acres, with talks covering 30,000 more, and the pair just hired a 16-year-old intern. “We want to create a resource that gives farmers the ability to do more with less water,” Trotta said.

title: 9,000 Malaysian students learned AI, and a vocational college team won with a smart-farming app
summary: More than 9,000 secondary students across Malaysia took part in AI Muda@NADI, a program launched in August with six online modules on prompting, responsible AI, and building apps. At the final hackathon, 26 teams pitched AI solutions for plantations and farming, and team INNOVIQ from Kolej Vokasional Perdagangan Johor Bahru won RM5,000 for TerraScan, an app that combines soil analysis, crop recommendations, weather forecasts, farm simulations, and financial tracking to cut costs and raise yields.

title: Tonight: a haunting Halloween concert at Cité des Arts
summary: The Gypsy Dawn Experience: Life Is Strange takes over Cité des Arts, 109 Vine St., tonight from 7:30 to 10 p.m., with doors at 6:30. It celebrates Gypsy Dawn’s debut album with original music and Halloween favorites, a magic-inspired tribal dance, a tarot reader, and vendors. Costumes encouraged. Also tonight, the Blue Moon Saloon’s weekly Cajun Jam starts at 8 p.m., per Lafayette Travel.

title: Tonight: free trunk-or-treat and fall festival at SoLAcc
summary: South Louisiana Community College hosts Soleil’s Fall Festival, a free, family-friendly event, today from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m. in Devalcourt Parking Lot D, 320 Devalcourt St., on its Lafayette campus. Expect trunk-or-treating, food trucks, inflatable games, and an appearance by Soleil, the college mascot. Costumes welcome.

title: Starting tonight: the free, family-friendly Chance Haunted Ride
summary: The Chance Haunted Ride, a family-friendly Halloween ride through two decorated 18-wheeler trailers and other displays, opens tonight at 303 Mill Valley Run and runs October 28 through 31, from 4 to 9 p.m. It’s free and open to the public. It started as a simple walk-through in 1995, and about 2,000 people visit each year.

title: Thursday: the UL Lafayette Symphony’s costumed Halloween Concert
summary: The UL Lafayette Symphony plays its annual Halloween Concert on Thursday, October 29, at 7 p.m. in Angelle Hall, with musicians in costume and the audience invited to dress up. The program includes a Star Wars medley, Night on Bald Mountain, and Haydn’s Surprise Symphony, plus dancers from The Ballet Studio. Admission is $10 for adults, children free; tickets are cash or check only at the door from 6 p.m.

title: This weekend: the Blackpot Festival & Cook-off takes over Vermilionville
summary: The South Louisiana Blackpot Festival & Cook-off runs from 6 p.m. Friday, October 30, through Saturday, October 31, at Vermilionville, 300 Fisher Road. Friday’s main stage opens with Diamond J and the Ruby Red Raindrops featuring Horace Trahan, then Tex Mex accordionist Josh Baca, with the Pine Leaf Boys closing, per Lafayette Travel. Saturday brings a full day of music, the cook-off, and a costume contest. Tickets on the festival site: $35 Friday night, $45 Saturday, or $70 for a weekend pass with camping, plus tax.

title: Halloween Saturday: the Amazing Nuns at Artmosphere and a costume party at the Blue Moon
summary: Halloween falls on Saturday, and Lafayette rock veterans the Amazing Nuns continue their long Halloween tradition at Artmosphere, with openers Hypno Nun and Jadder. Down the street, the Blue Moon Saloon’s party features New Natives Brass Band, Genuine Mustard, Kevin McCune, Trinity Reign, and the Mangoes, while Rock ’n’ Bowl hosts CRYRS for Emo Night, according to Lafayette Travel’s weekly music roundup.
